gaps.gap: Complaint hand-over: the trigger and the human are sourced (CPR 2.1.7, 26.7.2, licence 9.1); the mechanics are not (stop, hand over, how fast), and QoS T1(2a) measures only the wait after the IVR choice.

searched.says: The trigger: a communication becomes a Consumer Complaint the moment a Subscriber expresses dissatisfaction at any authorised place.
searched.quote: any correspondence or communication registered by any reasonable means at any place authorised by the Licensee for such purposes, from a Subscriber expressing dissatisfaction or grievance

searched.says: The Licensee App is a complaint channel.
searched.quote: any other licensee-developed channels such as by Licensee App., etc.

searched.says: 26.6 applies whichever Mandatory Channel is used (26.4.1 to 26.4.4 only).
searched.quote: apply in all cases regardless of which Mandatory Channel is used

searched.says: No non-human agents in complaint conversations; unqualified by channel. The Arabic reads 'excepted or excluded' (يستثنى أو يستبعد منها).
searched.quote: preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.

searched.says: A duty to help a Consumer formulate and lodge a complaint; no step for an automated channel.
searched.quote: reasonably assist any Consumer, so requesting such assistance, to formulate and to lodge a Consumer Complaint with the Licensee

searched.says: Trained personnel for complaints, at licence level, on every channel (Arabic: موظفين مدربين). No hand-over procedure or time.
searched.quote: The Licensee shall maintain adequate trained personnel to receive and respond promptly to complaints and disputes from Customers.

searched.says: Annex A, T1(2a): the only time measured is the wait after the IVR choice, under two minutes, indicative. A bot before that choice, and chat or app, are unmeasured.
searched.quote: Average time (seconds) spent waiting from the time the Customer has selected the IVR choice to speak to an agent until the Customer is connected to an agent

gaps.uae_position: The human requirement is binding (26.7.2, licence 9.1) and Mizan enforces it; no text says what an automated channel must do at the moment a conversation becomes a complaint, or how fast the human must take over.

gaps.line: consent elicited by an AI (channel classification)
gaps.gap: Consent elicited by an AI: the CPR medium classification (4.10, 4.17, 4.22) decides whether an OTP is needed, and PDPL 6(1)(b) names consent 'in writing or electronically', not spoken.

searched.says: Spoken consent is acceptable for a purchase if it can be stored.
searched.quote: all tangible forms of consent: written; spoken; and, electronic interaction are acceptable

searched.says: Digital applications: multi-step, 2FA unless expressly specified otherwise.
searched.quote: unless objectively justified otherwise, or expressly specified otherwise, the process shall require the consumer to complete a 2FA procedure

searched.says: Where 2FA is mandated, the default is an OTP.
searched.quote: the default method of 2FA shall, in the absence of any approved alternative, be one-time password (OTP).

searched.says: Call-centre purchases: recorded verbal consent, no 2FA. A voice agent reads naturally as this.
searched.quote: where a Service is purchased via a telephone call to/from a Licensee

searched.says: Licensee App purchases: no express 2FA. A chat agent in the app reads as this or as 4.10.
searched.quote: where the purchase of a Licensee provided Service3 is made via a Licensee App

searched.says: What an automated system sends is the operator's own act.
searched.quote: If it is sent by an electronic medium automated and programmed to operate automatically by or on behalf of the Originator.

searched.says: Data-processing consent in writing or electronically; spoken is not named.
searched.quote: whether in writing or electronically

gaps.uae_position: No CPR sales medium names a conversational agent, so whether an AI-elicited purchase needs an OTP depends on a classification no text makes; a spoken consent through the agent covers the purchase (4.7.2) but not a new processing purpose under PDPL 6(1)(b). Mizan takes the strict reading (4.10 plus OTP, 4.11).

gaps.gap: 'Adequate verification process' (CPR 24.10) is undefined for a remote channel; the Electronic Transactions Art 33 trust levels were never mapped to it.

searched.says: Disclose a Subscriber's own information after an adequate verification process; adequate is not defined.
searched.quote: the Licensee shall disclose it free of charge and without delay after an adequate verification process.

searched.says: Verification by security questions or the Licensee's own procedures.
searched.quote: by asking the relevant security questions, or by following such other procedures used by the Licensee for identification purposes

searched.says: Three trust levels, low, medium and high, for electronic identification.
searched.quote: The levels of security and trust of the Electronic Identification System and the Digital Identity issued thereby are three: low, medium and high

searched.says: TDRA sets authentication procedures; none mapped to CPR 24.10.
searched.quote: Authentication Procedures to confirm the identity of any person to the Relying Party.

searched.says: On a loss report the licensee verifies the reporter's identity; the method is not stated (Arabic only).

gaps.uae_position: A voice or chat agent that discloses account data after security questions is within the letter of the CPR; the national trust levels exist but no text says which level 24.10 needs on a remote channel.

global_examples.quote: shall specify assurance levels low, substantial and/or high for electronic identification means issued under that scheme.
the authentication mechanism, through which the natural or legal person uses the electronic identification means to confirm its identity to a relying party;

gaps.recommendation: TDRA to name the Art 33 trust level that an adequate verification process under 24.10 requires on a remote channel, as eIDAS Art 8 ties each assurance level to an authentication mechanism.
gaps.competitor_basis: its gap table lists 'no SIM-swap authentication rule', a different act (SIM swap, not disclosure of account data)

gaps.gap: Automated disconnection: PDPL 18(4) human review has no procedure, deadline or regulator; the 18(2) contract escape is undercut by Cabinet 66/2023 34(1), (3), (5) (inferred interaction, both quoted).

searched.says: A right to object to automated decisions with legal or adverse effect; disconnection meets it.
searched.quote: particularly those decisions which have legal impact on or adversely affect the Data Subject.

searched.says: No objection where the contract provides for the automated processing.
searched.quote: If the automated processing is agreed upon under the contract made between the Data Subject and the Controller.

searched.says: Human review on request, not conditioned on 18(1); no procedure, deadline or regulator.
searched.quote: The Controller shall include the human element in reviewing automated processing decisions at the request of the Data Subject.

searched.says: A prohibited term: the provider terminates unilaterally.
searched.quote: unilaterally terminate it without referring to the consumer

searched.says: A prohibited term: the provider alone judges conformity.
searched.quote: Authorising the provider to determine by himself and without referring to the consumer whether the goods or service subject of the contract is in conformity

searched.says: A prohibited term: unilateral change of a subscription, except a notified upgrade.
searched.quote: the right to unilaterally change the characteristics of the goods or the terms of the consumer use of the service in the case of services subscription contracts

gaps.uae_position: The right to a human review exists (18(4)); a contract term that lets the operator alone decide a disconnection is a prohibited term under 66/2023 34 (inferred interaction of the two texts); nothing says how the review runs, by when, or who enforces it, because the PDPL Executive Regulations were never issued.

global_examples.quote: at least the right to obtain human intervention on the part of the controller, to express his or her point of view and to contest the decision.

gaps.recommendation: UAE Data Office to issue the 18(4) review procedure: who reviews, the deadline, how the subscriber puts a point of view and contests, and which regulator hears a refusal.
gaps.competitor_basis: its gap table lists 'PDPL Art 18 right to object has no procedure' (hq reading notes 2026-10-17); differs from the order, which says no

gaps.gap: No binding UAE text sets conduct standards for an AI agent dealing with a consumer. The clauses that name AI or an automated agent set a charge waiver (CPR 25.14.1), a bar (26.7.2), a definition (Spam Calls v4 3.3(iii)), a permission (Cabinet 56/2024 5(6)) and a tool (Child Digital Safety 10(1)(g)); PDPL 18 and Electronic Transactions 11 to 13 govern automated decisions and contracts as outcomes, not the agent's conduct.

searched.says: Directory enquiries by an AIA: charges waived if it fails. A billing rule, not a conduct standard.
searched.quote: enquiry is processed by an artificial intelligence assistance (AIA)

searched.says: Non-human agents excluded from complaint conversations. A bar, not a conduct standard.
searched.quote: preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.

searched.says: Point (iii): a synthesised voice can make a Spam Call. A definition.
searched.quote: the audible message contains a natural or a synthesised voice

searched.says: Automated systems may market. A permission.
searched.quote: Automated communication systems may be used for marketing

searched.says: Point (g): platforms may use AI to detect harmful content. A tool, not a standard for AI conduct.
searched.quote: including artificial intelligence systems and machine learning algorithms, for proactive detection, removal, or reporting thereof

searched.says: The controller adds a human to the review of an automated processing decision when the data subject asks. A rule for the decision, not for the agent's conduct.
searched.quote: The Controller shall include the human element in reviewing automated processing decisions at the request of the Data Subject.

searched.says: An automated system can make a contract if the other person knows, or should know, it is automated. A rule for the contract, not for the agent's conduct.
searched.quote: if the latter knows, or is supposed to know, that such system will make or execute the contract automatically.

searched.says: A document sent by an automated medium on the originator's behalf is the originator's. Attribution of the outcome, not a conduct standard.
searched.quote: If it is sent by an electronic medium automated and programmed to operate automatically by or on behalf of the Originator.

searched.says: Table No. (1), row 16: a fine for using automatic calling or marketing in breach of Cabinet 56/2024 (Clause (6)). A penalty, not a conduct standard.
searched.quote: 16 Using automatic calling or marketing

gaps.uae_position: The binding texts read name AI or an automated agent to set a charge waiver, a bar, a definition, a permission and a tool; none sets how an AI agent must behave with a consumer. PDPL 18(4), Electronic Transactions 11(2) and 12(2) and Cabinet 57/2024 Table No. (1) row 16 govern automated decisions, contracts, documents and calls as outcomes, not the agent's conduct.

gaps.line: Y.3172 has no hand-over to a human
gaps.gap: Standards gap, addressed to ITU: Y.3172 has no node outcome for a hand-over to a human. The policy node applies policies to the model's output and the distributor sends it on to a sink that acts; no node routes it to a person.

searched.says: Clause 8.1 (pages 13 and 14) defines the nodes SRC, C, PP, M, P, D and SINK. P applies policies to the model's output; D distributes it to SINK nodes, which act on it. No node or outcome sends an output to a human.
searched.quote: P (policy): This node enables the application of policies to the output of the model node.

searched.says: The only mention of a human in the Recommendation's text (page 4): a SON example acting 'without human intervention'. The back-page list of ITU-T series names 'human factors' as a series title only.
searched.quote: without human intervention

standard_text.quote: P (policy): This node enables the application of policies to the output of the model node.
D (distributor): This node is responsible for identifying the SINK(s) and distributing the output of the M node to the corresponding SINK nodes.
SINK: This node is the target of the ML output on which it takes action.
give network design recommendations without human intervention.

gaps.uae_position: CPR 26.7.2 and licence 9.1 require a human in a complaint conversation; Mizan's P node gate returns a hand-over that Y.3172 has no outcome for, so it is mapped outside the standard's node set.
gaps.global_none: none; the recommendation is the example
gaps.recommendation: ITU-T to add a policy-node outcome that withholds the model's output and routes the case to a named human (hand-over), with its own reference point, so a regulator's human-in-the-loop rule maps into the pipeline.
gaps.competitor_basis: its README maps Y.3172 nodes and states no standards gap
